name: Negotiate master service agreements and pricing
summary: Before crews can work for a producer, the company needs a signed master service agreement that sets out who carries which risks, what insurance each side holds and how invoices are approved, plus a pricing schedule with the agreed rates. Producers usually push their own contract form, so the contract administrator marks deviations, legal counsel redlines the indemnities and insurance clauses, and redlines travel back and forth for weeks. Pricing schedules are renegotiated more often than MSAs, especially in 2021-2022 when fuel, sand and wage costs rose. Delays come from waiting on the producer's legal and supply chain staff, and errors come from rates and terms that are not carried correctly into the price book and to field and billing staff.

baseline.org_archetype: A listed Canadian pressure pumper of about 1,350 people with a small Calgary contracts and legal team and agreements with 60-plus producers.
baseline.notes: Most cases are pricing schedule renewals under an existing MSA; about 40% involve a new MSA or an amendment.

trigger: A producer awards work or asks to set up, renew or reprice its agreement with the company.
end_state: The MSA or amendment and the pricing schedule are signed by both parties, filed, loaded to the price book and briefed to operations and billing, or the negotiation is abandoned.

volume.seasonality: Pricing schedules cluster in the fourth and first quarters with annual awards; extra repricing rounds in 2021-2022 for cost inflation.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate; about 60 customers with a schedule or MSA change every one to two years.

surge.cause: Year-end and first-quarter repricing when annual awards and cost escalation take effect

evidence.note: Prices raised for all clients through Q4 2021 and into Q1 2022 (step-2021); multiplier tier C.
Intake, commercial review, pricing negotiation and briefing; about 4-5 hours per case.
Register, deviation marking, redline consolidation, signature routing and filing; about 7 hours per case.
Redline and counter-redline review on MSA cases; about 7 hours per MSA case.
Drafts the pricing schedule and any counter-proposals; about 5 hours per case. Not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Approvals of deviations and pricing.
Checks insurance clauses on MSA cases; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)

steps.name: Receive award and agreement request
steps.description: The account manager receives the award letter or the producer's request to set up or renew an agreement, together with the producer's own MSA form or pricing schedule template, and opens a contract request with the contract administrator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Check contract register
steps.description: The contract administrator looks up the producer in the contract register to see whether a signed MSA exists, which version, its insurance and indemnity terms and when the current pricing schedule expires.

error.defect_description: An amended or superseded version is taken as current.

next.condition: no MSA, expired MSA or MSA amendment needed
MSA in place; pricing schedule only

evidence.note: Producer master agreements mostly do not expire but are amended when services or risk change (ovintiv-suppliers). Split tier C.

steps.name: Obtain the producer's MSA form
steps.description: The contract administrator asks the producer's contracts group for its current MSA form and schedules (insurance, safety, invoicing), and waits for the producer's sponsor to open the request on their side.

evidence.note: A producer sponsor must start supplier onboarding before an agreement is set up (ovintiv-suppliers).

steps.name: Wait for the producer's form
steps.description: The producer's contracts team sends its form and schedules, which are usually the producer's own paper rather than an industry template, and the contract administrator chases by email if nothing arrives within a week.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Mark deviations from standard positions
steps.description: The contract administrator compares the producer's form clause by clause with the company's standard positions and the PSAC model clauses, and marks deviations in indemnity, limits of liability, insurance, payment terms, price adjustment and warranty.

error.defect_description: A deviation buried in a schedule is missed.

evidence.note: PSAC 2017 template MSA and model clauses as a reference; negotiation turns on warranty, indemnity, IP, insurance and safety (bj-msa). Times tier C.

steps.name: Legal review and redline
steps.description: Legal counsel reviews the deviation list and the form, focusing on the knock-for-knock indemnities, carve-outs for well control, reservoir and downhole equipment losses, gross negligence, consequential loss and governing law, and drafts the company's redline.

error.defect_description: Redline misses a conflict with the company's insurance program.

control.basis: Contract review policy: legal counsel reviews every MSA and amendment before signature

evidence.note: Knock-for-knock risk allocation and the clauses that drive MSA negotiations (ablawg-k4k, bj-msa). Times tier C.

steps.name: Check insurance requirements
steps.description: The risk and insurance manager compares the required coverages, limits, additional insured and waiver of subrogation wording with the company's policies, and notes what the broker would need to change.

evidence.note: Insurance is one of the clauses that usually drives negotiation (bj-msa). Times tier C.

steps.name: Review commercial terms
steps.description: The account manager reviews payment terms, invoicing method (e-invoicing network, field ticket approval), price adjustment and standby clauses and decides which points matter to the customer relationship and which can be conceded.

evidence.note: Producer invoicing through an e-invoicing network (ovintiv-suppliers). Times tier C.

steps.name: Send redline to producer
steps.description: The contract administrator consolidates legal, insurance and commercial comments into one redline with a cover note and sends it to the producer's contracts contact.

error.defect_description: Wrong version of the redline sent.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Wait for producer response
steps.description: The producer's contracts and legal staff review the redline among many other suppliers' agreements and return a counter-redline or acceptance.

evidence.note: Organisation file says redlines go back and forth for weeks; timing tier C.

steps.name: Review counter-redline
steps.description: Legal counsel reads the producer's response, accepts reasonable compromises and decides whether the remaining gaps need another round, a call, or escalation.

next.condition: terms agreed or residual points minor
producer withdraws or company walks away

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Negotiation call
steps.description: Legal counsel and the account manager hold a call with the producer's contracts and legal staff to trade positions on the open clauses, then update the redline.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Approve residual deviations
steps.description: The vice president of sales, with legal advice, accepts any remaining non-standard risk terms in writing under the delegation of authority, or rejects them.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: VP sales and general counsel approve non-standard indemnity or liability terms

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Draft customer pricing schedule
steps.description: The pricing analyst builds the customer pricing schedule from the bid or the current price book: discounts by service line, standby and mobilisation rates, pass-through rules for sand, trucking and fuel, and a cost escalation clause.

error.defect_description: Rate or discount differs from the awarded bid.

evidence.note: Prices raised with clients to offset inflation in 2021-2022 (step-2021). Times tier C.

steps.name: Negotiate the pricing schedule
steps.description: The account manager sends the schedule to the producer's supply chain lead, walks through changes from the last schedule (fuel, sand, wage increases) and agrees or concedes items.

evidence.note: Working with clients to raise prices for inflation (step-2021). Times tier C.

steps.name: Wait for producer pricing response
steps.description: The producer's supply chain team compares the schedule with other suppliers and its budget and replies with acceptance or a counter-proposal.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Approve pricing schedule
steps.description: The vice president of sales checks the agreed rates against margin floors and signs the internal approval for the schedule.

control.basis: Sales delegation of authority: pricing below standard margin

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Route for signature
steps.description: The contract administrator prepares execution copies of the MSA or amendment and the pricing schedule, obtains the company signature from an authorised officer and sends them to the producer.

error.defect_description: Execution copy does not match the agreed redline.

control.basis: Signing authority: only named officers sign customer agreements

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Wait for producer countersignature
steps.description: The producer's authorised signatory countersigns and returns the agreement, often through its own contract or e-signature system, after the producer's internal approvals; the contract administrator chases if it is not back within two weeks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: File agreement and update register
steps.description: The contract administrator files the executed documents, records the version, term, insurance limits and pricing schedule dates in the contract register, and sends the insurance certificate if requested.

error.defect_description: Expiry date or limits entered wrong.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Request price book update
steps.description: The contract administrator sends the executed pricing schedule to the price book team so the customer's rates and discounts are loaded into the ERP price book and field ticket app before the next job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

steps.name: Brief operations and billing
steps.description: The account manager emails the district managers, program planners and billing a summary of the terms that change field work and invoicing: standby rules, approved pass-throughs, ticket approval and invoicing method.

error.defect_description: A billing-relevant term is left out, causing disputes on later invoices.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

exceptions.name: Several redline rounds
exceptions.description: The producer does not accept the company's indemnity or insurance positions and the parties hold further calls and rounds.

exceptions.name: Pricing counter-proposal
exceptions.description: The producer counters the pricing schedule, often resisting escalation for fuel or wages.

exceptions.name: Negotiation abandoned
exceptions.description: The parties cannot agree on risk terms and the award lapses or work continues under the old agreement.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from award or request to agreement briefed
benchmarks.population: MSA and pricing schedule cases at a Canadian service company, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Estimate: a pricing schedule under an existing MSA takes two to five weeks; a new MSA with redlines six to twelve weeks.

pain_points.description: Producers push their own forms, so each MSA needs a clause-by-clause comparison and several redline rounds on indemnity and insurance.

evidence.note: Clauses that drive negotiation (bj-msa) and knock-for-knock allocation (ablawg-k4k).

pain_points.description: Agreed rates reach the price book and the field by email; wrong or late loading leads to invoice disputes.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

pain_points.description: Most elapsed time is spent waiting on the producer's contracts and supply chain staff.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for MSA and pricing schedule negotiation between Canadian service companies and producers in 2019-2022; no source gives step times.

sources.title: Master Service Agreements in the Oilfield Services Industry
sources.publisher: Bennett Jones LLP (K. Iatridis and G. Stenger)
sources.supports: MSA negotiations in oilfield services usually turn on warranties and remedies, liability and indemnification, intellectual property, insurance, and health and safety; PSAC published a template MSA and handbook of model clauses in 2017.

sources.title: Alberta Decision on Knock-for-Knock Allocation of Liability in a Standard Form Drilling Contract
sources.publisher: ABlawg (Nigel Bankes), University of Calgary Faculty of Law
sources.supports: Knock-for-knock (each party bears its own losses regardless of fault) in the CAPP/CAODC standard form; Alberta court enforced it between sophisticated parties.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Tight supply of field staff, limits on how fast recruits can be added safely, rising labour cost; prices raised for all clients in Q4 2021 and Q1 2022 to offset inflation; crews booked through Q1; spring break-up affects Canadian operations; extreme cold caused delays.

sources.title: Supplier Resources
sources.supports: A producer requires an ISNetworld PASS grade for field suppliers, a company sponsor before an agreement is set up, master agreements that mostly do not expire but are amended when services or risk change, and invoicing through OpenInvoice.

assumptions: Loaded costs are the organisation file's (base wage x 1.35).
The pricing analyst and the risk and insurance manager take part although the organisation file's process map does not list them for this process.

The trigger is split between awards from the company's own tender responses and producer requests to renew or reprice outside a tender; the executed agreement also goes to billing (fin-field-ticket-to-invoice), which the process map does not show.

Legal review is described inside this workflow; lg-contract-review is treated as the standing legal input and the place where executed agreements are filed, to avoid counting the same legal hours twice.
No public source on agreement cycle times was found; all times and branch shares are tier C.
